subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw core support beyond the shipped `/tools/invoke`, `tools.invoke`, SDK, and cron `command` paths, and what owner, config, audit, and proof gates are required for host filesystem, exec, slash/CLI, and cron tool-call payloads?
rationale: The remaining work can expose privileged filesystem, process, session, Gateway, cron, and node actions without a model turn, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent boundary or gate shape.

options.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
options.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing the active host-FS pull requests and require explicit owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Limit support to shipped paths
options.body: Declare HTTP/RPC/SDK direct invoke plus cron command payloads sufficient and reject or defer host-FS, exec, slash, CLI, and generic cron tool-call dispatch until a maintainer-sponsored proposal exists.

options.title: Approve broader direct execution
options.body: Allow broader direct tool execution only after a named security design defines operator-facing controls, upgrade behavior, and proof requirements.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing the active host-FS pull requests and require explicit owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The open decision is primarily the dangerous-tool and owner-gated Gateway security boundary, and recent history ties steipete to that boundary.
